findings.text: follow-on: no case discriminates reservation_occupancy from occupancy; every scenario sits at or below the 28 admitted cores (scenario 1 is 20 live of which 1 placed, scenarios 2-3 place every live pointer), so reverting the placed-only threading at reckon/crew/summary.py:368 to use occupancy leaves all four cases green. Measured directly against the landed module: cores_bound(occupancy=20, reservation_occupancy=20) and cores_bound(occupancy=20, reservation_occupancy=1) both admit, and only occupancy >= 29 separates them, so the done-when's second clause (count only placed live workers) is implemented but unguarded.

follow-on: _reservation_admitted_cores reads the unkeyed record through read_reservation() with no project, while the sibling roster refusal at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:578 reads read_reservation(project) and honours the legacy per-project fallback, so during migration a project holding only a legacy reservation is roster-bounded yet reports the cores bound unknown; the two readers of the one shared record disagree about which record is the shared one.
